fields.name: Harirāma Vyāsa
fields.place: Oṛchā (Bundelkhand); Vṛndāvana: Kiśora-vana («Vyāsajī kā gherā»), where he and his wife have their samādhis
fields.works: Svadharma-paddhati; Navaratna (on the nine prameyas of Madhvācārya); vāṇī / padāvalī (with his wife)
fields.notes: Brāhmaṇa of Oṛchā, disciple of Mādhava, in the line of Mādhavendra Purī (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Harirāma Vyāsa»; not Harirāma Ācārya, the disciple of Rāmacandra Kavirāja). Driven from home by his brothers for feeding Vaiṣṇavas and taking prasāda from low-caste Hāḍis, he settled in Vṛndāvana with his wife (Bhaktamāla 20). Tore off his sacred thread to tie the ankle-bell of the boy playing Rādhā in a rāsa-līlā. His wife built the temple of Yugala-kiśora (Naval-kiśora) with the money of her ornaments; some say he found the Deity in a well at Kiśora-vana. Akbar is said to have given him lands.
